name: of1
philosophy: of1 wins by reframing personalization from a complex technical problem into an inevitable truth. While competitors sell segmentation engines and audience platforms, of1 sells the end of audiences as a concept — every person becomes their own audience. It's not better personalization. It's the death of impersonal.

variants.name: of1 on dark
variants.usage: Primary usage — dark backgrounds (black #0A0A0A). Wordmark in cream #F5F0E8.

variants.name: of1 on red
variants.usage: Accent contexts. Wordmark in black #0A0A0A on red #FF3D00.

logo.clearSpace: Minimum clear space equal to the height of the '1' character on all sides.
donts: Never separate 'of' and '1' with a space
Never use a font other than JetBrains Mono Bold for the wordmark

primary.name: Black
primary.role: Primary background. The dominant surface — dark mode is the brand's natural state.

primary.name: Cream
primary.role: Primary text on dark. Secondary background for light sections. Warm, not white.

primary.name: Red
primary.role: Primary accent. CTAs, italic display accents, eyebrows on light backgrounds, tagline. The signal fire.

secondary.name: Blue
secondary.role: Secondary accent. Interactive states, structural voice tags, link hovers. Electric, not corporate.

secondary.name: Mint
secondary.role: Tertiary accent. Success states, positive indicators, highlighted key phrases, 'say this' examples. Calm energy.

web.name: Black
web.role: Page background, button text on colored backgrounds

web.name: Cream
web.role: Body text on dark, section backgrounds on light

web.name: Red
web.role: Primary CTA background, accent text, hover states

web.name: Mint
web.role: Highlighted text, success states, eyebrows on dark

borderRadius.usage: Cards, type specimens, wordmark containers — consistent rounding across all contained elements.

patterns.name: Primary (red)
patterns.style: background: #FF3D00; color: #0A0A0A; border-radius: 100px; padding: 0.5rem 1.5rem; font: JetBrains Mono 600 0.55rem; letter-spacing: 0.15em; text-transform: uppercase

patterns.name: Primary (dark)
patterns.style: background: #0A0A0A; color: #F5F0E8; border-radius: 100px; padding: 0.5rem 1.5rem; font: JetBrains Mono 600 0.55rem; letter-spacing: 0.15em; text-transform: uppercase

motifs.name: High-contrast editorial minimalism
motifs.description: Generous negative space interrupted by bold typographic statements. Dark mode dominant with warm cream accents. No gradients, no glassmorphism, no safe corporate blue.
motifs.usage: Foundational layout principle. Every section breathes. Content is the ornament.

motifs.name: Signal Fire palette
motifs.description: Named color palette — the combination of black, cream, and red evokes urgency and conviction, like a signal fire in darkness.
motifs.usage: The three-color core (black/cream/red) should dominate. Blue and mint are punctuation, not co-stars.

motifs.name: Serif italic accent
motifs.description: Single words in Cormorant Garamond italic + red within mono or display headlines. Creates a visual catch — the literary voice breaking through the engineered voice.
motifs.usage: One word per headline maximum. The italic word is the emotional pivot of the sentence. e.g. 'The end of *audiences.*'

motifs.name: Pill-shaped elements
motifs.description: Buttons and tags use border-radius: 100px — fully rounded capsules. Tone tags, CTAs, and category labels all share this shape.
motifs.usage: All interactive elements and classification tags. Never use square or slightly-rounded buttons.

motifs.name: Faint dividers
motifs.description: Section borders at rgba(245,240,232,0.06) — barely visible, felt more than seen.
motifs.usage: Between all major sections. The brand relies on negative space and faint structure, not heavy rules.

heading.usage: Headlines, statements, pull quotes — the literary voice. Display text that makes declarations.

subheading.usage: Section subheads, card titles, voice rule headers. The engineered voice at medium scale.

body.usage: Body text, descriptions, explanatory copy. Deliberately subdued against dark backgrounds — the brand lets headlines carry the weight.

accent.usage: Single-word italic accents within headlines, colored red (#FF3D00). One word per headline max. The word is the emotional pivot.

eyebrow.usage: Section labels, category tags. Tiny (0.5-0.55rem), wide letter-spacing (0.3-0.35em), subdued opacity. Structural, not decorative.

button.usage: CTA labels. Uppercase, 0.55rem, 0.15em letter-spacing. Capsule-shaped buttons.

rules: Sentence case for all headings — never Title Case or ALL CAPS except eyebrows
Em dashes (—) preferred over en dashes or hyphens for parenthetical breaks
Cormorant Garamond italic accent limited to one word per headline, always in red

photography.style: Abstract, high-contrast, editorial. Dark environments with warm light. No stock photography of smiling people at laptops.
rules: Prefer abstract/conceptual imagery over literal product screenshots
Dark backgrounds consistent with brand palette
If people appear, they are silhouetted or partially obscured — the brand is about the visitor, not the marketer
Warm color temperature — cream, amber, fire tones against dark
donts: No bright white backgrounds in photography
No group shots of diverse teams pointing at screens
No literal AI imagery (robots, neural networks, glowing brains)
photography.social: Same dark editorial aesthetic. Quote cards use the manifesto voice — short, declarative, one statement per card.

voice.character: Manifesto. Bold declarations. Short sentences. Poetic rhythm. Speaks from conviction. Doesn't ask permission. The voice of someone who has already seen the future and is calmly explaining it to you.

do.text: The end of audiences. The beginning of everyone.
do.context: Hero headline — staccato contrast, big claim delivered calmly

do.text: We made your website pay attention — so every visitor finds exactly what they came for, as if it had always been there.
do.context: Key line — long sentence with em dash break, ends on an intimate image

do.text: Most AI wants you to know it's there. Ours wants you to forget.
do.context: AI positioning — subverts the expectation, speaks through contrast
Provocative reframe — turns industry language against itself

do.text: Your website just becomes — quietly, impossibly — relevant.
do.context: Product description — parenthetical rhythm, ends on the brand's replacement word

do.text: Every person is a market of one.
do.context: Brand value — simple declaration, the philosophy in one line

do.text: Not a recommendation engine in a box.
do.context: Anti-positioning — says what it isn't to define what it is

dont.text: Our AI-powered personalization engine delivers optimized experiences.
dont.context: Violates three word rules at once — 'AI-powered', 'personalization', 'optimized'

dont.text: Seamless integration with your existing tech stack!
dont.context: 'Seamless integration' is banned. Exclamation mark is banned. Says nothing.

dont.text: Next-gen segmentation for the modern marketer.
dont.context: 'Next-gen' is banned. 'Segmentation' is what the brand is ending, not improving.

dont.text: Boost conversions with cutting-edge AI technology.
dont.context: Pure jargon. 'Cutting-edge', 'boost conversions' — this is everyone else's copy.

dont.text: of1 is the industry-leading personalization platform.
dont.context: Self-important, generic. The brand never calls itself a 'platform' or claims leadership.

rules: Never say 'AI-powered' — say what it does
Always subvert, never adopt, industry jargon
Name features for what the visitor experiences, not how it works
Marketing pages: staccato fragments + long-then-short contrast
Editorial and docs: measured prose — match structure to the job

tone.description: Context-dependent. Marketing surfaces use manifesto rhythm — staccato declarations, long-then-short contrasts, single italic accent words. Editorial and documentation use measured, precise prose. The conviction is constant; the cadence adapts.

writingGoals.description: Reframe the familiar. Make the reader question what they accepted. 'Segments are a confession.'
Speak to one person, not an audience. The irony is intentional — a brand about one-to-one speaks one-to-one.
Complex technology described in human terms. What it feels like, not how it works. 'Your site pays attention.'

cleverVsClear.clever: Headlines, taglines, hero copy, social cards. The manifesto voice. Rhythm and subversion.
cleverVsClear.clear: Product explanations, documentation, onboarding. Precise prose. No clever for its own sake.

contentPillars.name: The death of impersonal
contentPillars.description: The philosophical position — why segments, cohorts, and audiences are an admission of failure.

contentPillars.name: Invisible technology
contentPillars.description: The product truth — AI that disappears behind the experience. No badges, no spinners, no novelty.

contentPillars.name: The visitor's experience
contentPillars.description: Always told through the end user's eyes. The marketer is the buyer, but the visitor is the protagonist.

contentPillars.name: Effortless for everyone
contentPillars.description: Zero config for the brand, zero friction for the visitor. Complexity is the product's problem, not the customer's.

personas.name: The disillusioned marketer
personas.description: Forward-thinking marketing leader tired of segmentation theater. Has tried Dynamic Yield, Optimizely, Adobe Target. Knows the promise. Knows the gap. Wants true 1:1 without the complexity tax.
personas.motto: I don't want to build audiences. I want to reach people.
